summary: The article profiles the family of Alpine skiing star Mikaela Shiffrin, tracing how her parents Eileen and Jeff met in 1985 and built a skiing-centered family. It covers her upbringing in Vail, her training at Burke Mountain Academy, and her father's death on February 2, 2020 after a head injury from a fall. It also describes how Shiffrin, with her mother and brother Taylor, grieved and returned to racing.
one_line: Profile of Mikaela Shiffrin's family, from her parents' ski-rooted love story to her father Jeff's death in 2020 and her return to racing.
key_facts: Mikaela Shiffrin is the second child of Eileen and Jeff Shiffrin.
Eileen and Jeff met in 1985 at St. Elizabeth's Medical Center in Brighton, Massachusetts; Eileen was a nurse and Jeff an anesthesiologist completing his cardiothoracic rotation.
Eileen and Jeff married in 1986 and moved to Vail five years later, after being drawn to the snowy trails of Aspen.
Brother Taylor was born in 1992 and Mikaela in 1995.
When Taylor was 9 and Mikaela was 7, their parents enrolled them in Ski Club Vail, where Rika Moore began coaching them.
At 14, Mikaela swept most of the wins at the Topolino races in Italy.
Jeff's rules for Mikaela, "Be nice. Think first. Have fun," are affixed to the back of her helmet.
Taylor Shiffrin won two NCAA team titles with the University of Denver.
From 2011, Eileen became Mikaela's full-time traveling companion and handled her schoolwork, while Jeff handled logistics and used his PTO to visit.
Jeff Shiffrin died on February 2, 2020, after sustaining a head injury in an accidental fall, days after the family spent time together in Lake Garda, Italy.
Taylor told his grieving sister "You can't quit on us" and recalled their dad's phrase "When you're going through hell, keep going. Don't stop".
Mikaela returned to racing in 2021 at the first of two slalom races at Levi.
In 2022 she set the record for most World Cup wins in Alpine skiing history and thanked her dad on Instagram: "Dad, I hope you had a good view."
Shiffrin has two Olympic golds, five overall World Cup titles, and four world championship wins, and is the youngest Olympic Alpine slalom champion.
